# On bubbletea a `flex` child a loop renders takes its share of the Layout
# where it is a focus stop too, and is still the stop its place in the
# document makes it. Before, it was joined at its own size: the closure that
# sizes it runs after its later siblings render, and would have counted its
# copies after theirs, drawing the focus on `a!` where Tab says `a`.
#
# `app.sngl` writes the stops under a `for`; `shown.sngl` writes them out,
# and the two snapshots must be one screen, the focus on `a` in both.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1
sngl test --platform=bubbletea app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea shown.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'
cmp app.sngl.snapshots/shown.ansi shown.sngl.snapshots/shown.ansi
grep '^> a {32}a! {3}b {31}b! {3}end' app.sngl.snapshots/shown.ansi

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var names = ["a", "b"]

component row ui.node {
    ui.hbox(style={gap=8px}) {
        for var n = names {
            ui.button(text=n, style={flex=1})
            ui.button(text=n + "!")
        }
        ui.button(text="end")
    }
}

func testShown(t test.Test, c row) {
    t.snapshot("shown")
}

ui.window {
    row
}
-- shown.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component row ui.node {
    ui.hbox(style={gap=8px}) {
        ui.button(text="a", style={flex=1})
        ui.button(text="a!")
        ui.button(text="b", style={flex=1})
        ui.button(text="b!")
        ui.button(text="end")
    }
}

func testShown(t test.Test, c row) {
    t.snapshot("shown")
}

ui.window {
    row
}
